plan.readiness: The plan is mostly well defined, and its weakest part is the most important one. Every speaker screen and every coach screen has a locked prototype with exact sizes, timings and signed words: the Ideal Text page, the Feedback walk, the recording screens, consent and settings, and the coach panel. A builder can do most of the screen work without asking anything. The open questions are about where the locks meet. They are (a) one-slide prototypes against multi-slide Takes, (b) older locks against the 6 Oct walk lock and (c) server rules the coach panel would break: answering once, the rule that an error must have a definition, and keeping clearer versions out of the library. Fifteen questions settle all of them. Q-B14 and Q-B15 group the small look and behaviour choices so you can approve them in one tap. Some conflicts are already settled by the precedence rules and are not asked again. Because the walk lock wins, there is no coach dot, no pulse and one loader. Because the coach should never be waited on, an exercise with no coach video shows the library video. The F1-CORE engine is less well defined. V3 is built and served, but nobody measures transcription accuracy or word-to-slide accuracy. The rewrite lane is almost always empty, and coverage and empty lanes are only written to logs. V4 is fully signed in principle (M1-M10, P1-P6, V1-V22, the exit gate), but it has no code yet. It also has three open points: the role list (O1), the cut-off for falling back to V3 (O2), and written definitions for the words part of willfidence (O3). It also clashes with SPEC §17's 'never a ranking term'. Q-B1 settles that clash. That is why Wave 1 measures and fixes the core first, and why V4 starts measuring in Wave 2 before the walk is switched on. Three older 'decided' items have been overtaken by later locks: H5 (walk after V4), H8 (two coach sheets) and the N55 consent change. They are taken in through Q-B8 and Q-B15 and are not silently dropped. Migrations and every locked screen stay in this session, where the GPT check and the side-by-side picture check happen. Self-contained tests, copy constants, proxy routes and tooling go to Grok prompts or new Fable sessions.

The flow, words, gesture numbers and keys match the 7 Oct lock (#630/#631). Left: a 24px gap and a jumping loader, the strip spacing, pull-to-refresh on the mic screen, the Take 2 words timing, the close X, the 0.4 s fade and a committed browser test.

Words and main flows are built. Left: steps do not open at their top and have no fade-in, the welcome is cut off on short screens, the Support card has no copy button, Back from Privacy/Terms does not return to the same spot, the empty 'Your projects' cause is unproven, and the 0436 training fix is unverified in prod.

questions.q: May the machine use its private 'willfidence' read to choose which feedback to give?
questions.story: V4 picks the moment for feedback by multiplying how important the moment is by how much room it has to sound more assured. That needs the sound-times-words read, kept inside the machine and never shown. Your older spec says this read must never be used for ranking, and the words part needs a one-line written definition for each signal before it can exist. V4 cannot be built until this is settled.

options.label: Yes, inside the machine only
options.happens: I write one-line definitions of the four word signals and the list of moment roles (opening, key claim, …) for your signature. V4 then ranks with them, and nobody ever sees a number.

options.label: Sound only for now
options.happens: V4 ranks by the sound read alone until the word signals are defined. Simpler, but it is not the V4 you signed.

options.label: No
options.happens: V4 waits, and V3 stays as it is.

questions.q: With several slides, in what order does the Feedback walk go?
questions.story: The walk prototype has one slide. The lock says 'all the praise, then the practising, then Judgement time!', but not whether that spans the whole Take or one slide at a time. Every walk screen depends on this order.

options.label: Whole Take
options.happens: All praise from every slide, then all the practising, then one 'Judgement time!' for every moment. The top bar names each moment's slide.

options.label: Slide by slide, one judgement at the end
options.happens: Each slide's praise, then that slide's practising. One 'Judgement time!' at the end.

options.label: Slide by slide, all of it
options.happens: Each slide gets its own praise, practising and judgements.

questions.q: When the walk goes live, what does tapping a paragraph open?
questions.story: The walk lock says a tap opens that paragraph's feedback in the walk's look. Its prototype does not draw the 'This paragraph' screen (your answer, practise card, History) or the 'Helper words saved' screen from the 30 Sep lock, and it never says they are retired.

options.label: Walk for open moments, restyled screens for the rest
options.happens: A paragraph with an open moment opens the walk there. An answered or saved paragraph opens 'This paragraph' or 'Helper words saved', redrawn in the walk's look and keeping History and Edit.

options.label: Everything goes into the walk
options.happens: Both older screens are retired. History and Edit live only on the helper-words screen.

options.label: Keep today's screens beside the walk
options.happens: Two looks remain in the app.

questions.q: Are the words a locked prototype shows signed together with its design?
questions.story: Builders may only use signed words. Some words appear on locked prototypes but not on any signed list: 'All answered · 3 Takes', 'Camera', 'Kept: …' on the coach panel; the 'Journal' label above the post in the walk; 'Getting your mic ready' shown as text on the recording screen (today it is read only by screen readers).

options.label: Yes, signed with the design
options.happens: Everything a locked prototype shows is signed. Where a signed list differs, the list wins ('Choose a file'). Signed words with no place are not used. 'Journal' shows and the mic text becomes visible.

options.label: Send me a list first
options.happens: I put every such word on one page for you to sign word by word before those screens are built.

questions.q: With tap-by-tap picking, must the helper words sit next to each other?
questions.story: You chose 'each tap adds one word' (QA4 A). The new walk picker lets you pick any four words anywhere, but the server stores one phrase and the text marks helper words as one italic run. Both pickers must follow one rule.

options.label: One connected phrase
options.happens: Each tap adds a word next to the others, up to four, saved and shown in italics exactly as today.

options.label: Any four words anywhere
options.happens: Words can be scattered. The server and the italic marking must be redesigned first, which delays the picker.

options.label: Keep the two-tap rule
options.happens: Tap the first word, then the last.

questions.q: Sharing a Take: is it still asked after Skip, which agreement version applies, and how is it taken back?
questions.story: Your answer WQ1 A says Skip on 'Judgement time!' finishes the walk, but the locked prototype's Skip goes to the sharing question. CM2 B says sharing goes live at once, but the server refuses every share until a policy version is named. Consent must be withdrawable, yet no locked screen reopens it for a past Take.

options.label: Ask after Skip; today's terms; a 'Sharing' row
options.happens: Skip clears the bars, then still asks to share, then the end card. The current Privacy/Terms (which already have the community sections) is named, and each share records the words the speaker saw. A 'Sharing' row in the ⋯ menu reopens the same screen, and 'None' takes it back (that one word needs your signature).

options.label: No question after Skip; new terms; a list in settings
options.happens: Skip goes straight to the end card. New Terms are published and accepted first. Shared Takes are listed on Data & consent, which needs a prototype.

questions.q: When a coach names a new error in one field, what is it until it has a definition?

The locked screen asks only for a name, and the coach names it after seeing the machine's read, so it is not blind. This also decides which errors the coach can choose from.

The list shows every active error plus coach-named ones. Naming is a signal for you only, and readiness still comes from the blind check.

options.label: The model drafts it

questions.q: Where do V4's blind coach questions and 'listen again' go on the locked coach panel?

questions.q: After the walk, what bars and buttons does the text page show?

questions.q: During judging, how many other people's clips does the speaker hear, and what happens to the old 'Lend your ear'?

questions.q: If a coach taps 'Change my answer' after the speaker already got it, what does the speaker see?
questions.story: Today an answer can never be changed (the database refuses), but the locked panel has 'Change my answer'. The server must change, and someone has to decide what happens to the card the speaker already has.

questions.q: What goes into the exercise library from a coach's answer?
questions.story: Your September answer says a clearer version never goes to the library, because it is one speaker's own words. questions.q: May I apply these five small look choices as recommended?
questions.story: Each locked design draws a few details differently, or does not draw them at all. options.label: Yes, all five as listed
options.happens: Built as listed, with each screen shown to you in the Done list before it goes live.

options.label: One by one

questions.q: May I apply these smaller behaviour and wording choices as recommended?

Those stay in Earlier Takes.' with the real Take number; (2) an exercise with no coach video shows the library video, or goes straight to practise; (3) the reason lines B10-B12 are not shown for now; (4) the 'done before' mark is dropped, since the walk design has no place for it; (5) the Lounge's Take 3 message loses its last sentence; (6) corpus hide, delete and restore move to your admin area, and the import goes on with the new corpus screens; (7) 'Do you hear it?' stays on; (8) deleting a single project stays off; (9) 'What's changed since you agreed' stays as signed; (10) an empty project list says 'No projects yet.'; (11) a refused 'Turn on' keeps today's words, and we log the reason; (12) when counsel clears N55, the Personalised practice tick goes, after you sign the changed prototype.

build_waves.wave: Wave 1: fix and measure the core (no answers needed)
build_waves.goal: Measure transcription and slide bucketing, make paragraph identity and the rewrite and praise lanes trustworthy, record coverage, and fix the recording, consent and Ideal Text gaps that need no decision. Build the shared screenshot harness and the engines the walk needs.

build_waves.wave: Wave 2: V4 starts measuring; the walk's plan and line keys (after Q-B1, Q-B2, Q-B4, Q-B6, Q-B8, Q-B15)
build_waves.goal: V4 Phase 1 runs dark for every speaker, with pick logging, the random 20%, willfidence-v1, the practise read, rise per pick, vote counts, the dark picker and the coach sheets. Meanwhile the walk gets its plan builder, signed line keys and sharing backend.

build_waves.wave: Wave 3: the Feedback walk behind its switch (after Q-B3, Q-B5, Q-B9, Q-B10, Q-B11, Q-B14)
build_waves.goal: Build every walk screen on real data behind NEXT_PUBLIC_FEEDBACK_WALK, along with the matching Ideal Text, recording and settings changes. Each screen is pictured for your Done list.

build_waves.wave: Wave 4: the coach panel redesign and the reached bar (after Q-B7, Q-B12, Q-B13)
build_waves.goal: Write the coach panel plan. Make the server accept a diagnosis, a named error and a changed answer. Build every locked coach screen behind NEXT_PUBLIC_COACH_PANEL_V2, and calibrate V4's reached bar from blind coach answers.

build_waves.wave: Wave 5: switches on, each after your approval
build_waves.goal: Switch on the walk and the coach panel after you approve the pictures, then the corpus import, then V4 once its exit gate passes. Remove the old paths after a clean run and prepare the N55 consent change.

extra_questions.q: The Feedback-walk design says orange is used only for new words and the Lounge's 'new' tag. The text page also uses orange for the bars, the helper-word headline (page, Presentation Mode, export) and 'Something else' on the coach panel. Which stays orange?

options: A: The 'orange only for new words' rule applies inside the walk's screens only. Bars, helper-word headlines and 'Something else' stay orange.
B: Apply it everywhere: helper-word headlines turn black and bold, and bars use another colour.
C: Keep orange for helper words and the Lounge's 'new' only; bars become grey and green.

extra_questions.q: Your V4 plan adds two blind coach screens ('Pick the moment for feedback' and 'Which sounds surer'). The locked coach panel shows only 'Do you hear it?' and 'Pick the most confident moment'. Where do the V4 screens go?

B: Replace 'Pick the most confident moment' with 'Pick the moment for feedback', and add 'Which sounds surer' later.
C: Keep them off the coach panel; only you answer them in the admin area for now.

extra_questions.q: Before communities existed, the app had a separate 'share this clip' switch on Voice Album moments and a 'Lend your ear' step where speakers judge others' clips. Both are built but have no screen. What happens to them now that sharing is asked per Take in the walk?
extra_questions.why: Two sharing consents and two listening queues would confuse people and double the consent records.
options: A: Retire the Album share switch, Lend your ear and Bold voices. Communities (per-Take sharing, judging in the walk) are the only way.
B: Keep Lend your ear as the engine behind judging others in the walk, but use only the per-Take community consent.
C: Keep both as they are.

extra_questions.q: When practise becomes part of the service (your 6 Oct answer), the locked consent screens still show the optional 'Personalised practice' tick and the switch on Data & consent. What should happen to those screens once counsel approves the new Privacy and Terms?
extra_questions.why: The consent screens were locked on 7 Oct exactly as they are, and removing the tick changes a locked screen.
options: A: Remove the tick and the switch then; 'Three things to confirm' goes back to two items. I'll show you the changed prototype to sign first.
B: Keep the tick as an information line with no box.
C: Keep everything until you decide again.

extra_questions.q: On 6 Oct you asked for a 'done before' mark on the practise card (QA10 A). The locked walk says the practise screen has no title, no slide bar and no helper text. Where should 'done before' go?

options: A: Drop it; the walk's design wins.
B: Put it on the exercise-video screen before practising, as one small grey line you sign.

extra_questions.q: You signed three 'listen again' lines for coaches (when a speaker's answer disagrees). Where on the locked coach panel does that request appear?

B: As a third item under 'Also waiting · blind'.

B: Drop the last sentence entirely.

audits.tightness_why: The page, the paragraph overlay, the helper-words overlay and the words are drawn down to the screen by the Final Screens prototype and the build-list mocks, and signed in the 30 Sep lock plus N48. A builder could do most items with no questions. The gaps come from the 6 Oct walk lock: it wins over everything above and says 'one look everywhere', but its prototype draws only the walk. It does not say whether 'This paragraph' and 'Helper words saved' survive. Its page shows bars coloured by the speaker's answers and a 'Review feedback' link after the walk, which conflicts with B7 and D8. QA4 A (tap by tap) does not say whether the words must be next to each other. Q8's 'Take 1 note' names a sentence that does not fit the picker it is placed on. These need the founder before the restyle; the rest is mechanical.

questions.q: When the Feedback walk goes live, what should a tap on a paragraph open?
questions.why: The walk lock says 'tapping a paragraph opens that paragraph's feedback' and that its look is used everywhere, but its prototype has no 'This paragraph' screen (your judgement label, practise card, History) and no 'Helper words saved' stop. The 30 Sep lock (B5, B8, D6) built exactly those screens. The walk lock wins where they disagree, but it never says they are retired.
options: A: A paragraph with an open moment opens the walk at that moment. An answered or saved paragraph opens 'This paragraph' or 'Helper words saved', redrawn in the walk's look (full screen, grey picture, motion), and keeps History and Edit.
B: Every tap goes into the walk. 'This paragraph' and 'Helper words saved' are retired, and History and Edit live only on the helper-words screen.
C: Keep today's paragraph screens unchanged beside the new walk.

questions.q: After the walk is finished, what bars does the text show?
questions.why: Your 30 Sep lock (B7) colours bars by the machine's read, and a bar leaves once the moment is answered. The walk prototype's last page colours bars by your own answers (green after Yes or In-between, orange otherwise). Before the walk it shows bars only on the moments to practise, not on praise.
options: A: As locked on 30 Sep. Bars show only open moments, green or orange by the machine's read, and clear once answered.
B: As the walk prototype draws. After the walk, every answered paragraph keeps a bar coloured by the speaker's own answer.
C: No bars at all once the walk is done.

questions.q: What sits at the bottom of the text once nothing is waiting?
questions.why: The walk prototype shows a black '● Record Take N' with a grey 'Review feedback' link under it, so the walk can be reopened. Today the app shows only 'Record Take N', plus a grey 'See next steps' link on Takes 1 to 3 that no prototype shows.
options: A: Exactly the walk prototype: '● Record Take N' and the 'Review feedback' link. 'See next steps' goes.
B: '● Record Take N', 'Review feedback' and, on Takes 1 to 3, 'See next steps'.
C: Keep today: 'Record Take N' and 'See next steps' only.

questions.q: With tap-by-tap picking (QA4 A), must the helper words be next to each other?
questions.why: The picker still uses the retired two-tap rule (tap the first word, tap the last). Tap by tap could mean 'grow one connected phrase' or 'any four words anywhere'. The walk prototype lets you pick scattered words, but the text marks helper words as one italic phrase.
options: A: Each tap adds the next word, and the words stay one connected phrase of up to four.
B: Any four words anywhere in the paragraph, saved as separate cues.
C: Keep the two-tap rule.

questions.q: Which note goes on the helper-words picker?
questions.why: Your 5 Oct answer says the 'Take 1 note' that shows in the paragraph's picker is 'These replace your Take 1 words. Those stay in Earlier Takes.' But that picker opens only on a paragraph that has no words yet, so there is nothing to replace. Today it shows 'These words show while you record your next take' on Take 1. The replace line appears on the helper-words screen with a changing Take number ('Take 2', 'Take 3').
options: A: Picker on Take 1: 'These words show while you record your next take'. Helper-words screen: 'These replace your Take N words. Those stay in Earlier Takes.', with N the Take the old words came from (sign the changing number).
B: Use the replace line only, exactly as signed ('Take 1'), and only when Take 1 words are being replaced.
C: Drop both notes.

questions.q: Should the paragraph keep the coach dot and the pulsing orange bar?
questions.why: Your 6 Oct answer QA6 A lit a coach dot on the bar. The walk lock, later the same day, moved the 'new' marker to the Lounge bubble ('the paragraph keeps only its bar') and says nothing blinks. Today the orange bar and an unread coach dot both pulse.
options: A: The bar alone: no dot and no pulse. New coach work shows only on the Lounge bubble.
B: Keep a still grey dot when a coach note exists, with no pulse.
C: Keep today's dot and pulse.

questions.q: How should Presentation Mode look?
questions.why: The design frame shows a dark screen with the slide, the orange headline and the italic words. The app shows a light screen with a column of slide dots on the right. Your 5 Aug words were 'only the X ... nothing, just the presentation'.
options: A: Dark, as the frame shows, with no slide dots.
B: Light, as today, with no slide dots.
C: Keep today's light screen with the dots.

questions.q: While feedback is still arriving after a Take, what loading sign shows on the text?
questions.why: The Ideal Text design draws a thin moving line under the header. The walk lock says the app has one loading animation, the breathing voice mark.
options: A: Keep the thin line on the text page, and use the breathing mark only inside overlays.
B: Replace the line with a small breathing voice mark in the header.
C: Show nothing until the bars arrive.

audits.agreed_summary:
FILTER: ADVANCE-F1-SURFACE — cat F1-SURFACE (Feedback decisions surface; communities part is F2 peer provenance) — fences clear if built as locked (no number on any screen, judgements stay the speaker's own, coach blind untouched, live loop kept behind a switch) — locks clear (accepting a clearer version is the user's decision, L1; lines only from the signed bank, L2; peer/coach/owner/machine kept apart, L3) — redirect: none.

What is agreed (lock file + prototype v10, amended by later founder answers N53-N55, which win where they are newer): the walk opens as a full-screen overlay from "Review feedback" or a paragraph tap; order is coach's note for the Take (video then words) -> all praise moments, each followed by "Choose your helper words" (max 4) -> the practising (clearer version, exercise) -> "Judgement time!" -> the judgements (speaker's voice only, Yes / In-between / No big, Not sure / Audio unclear small, auto-advance with toast "Yes ✓" etc., WQ4 A) -> sharing after every finished review -> end card "Record Take N" / "Back to the text". Practise records at once on the Take's strip, no title/slide bar; the machine checks every try (never asks the speaker, never a number); praise ends the loop, otherwise "It was better, and I have yet another practice for you to try!" only when something moved (NX3 A) or one of four NX3a lines when nothing moved; at most 3 tries, then one of four CM3b lines and on to "Judgement time!" (CM3a A, amends D2 and the lock's 'until praise or Skip'). Skip on "Judgement time!" finishes the walk and clears the bars (WQ1 A). "Your coach is working on your exercise." is not shown in the walk (WQ2 B). With personalised practice off the clearer version offers "Accept" + "Keep my words" (WQ3 A / WQ3c A) until the Privacy/Terms change of N55 lands. One grey silhouette for coach and app, no photos, no sender labels (NX2 B). One player, one judgement screen, VoiceMark as the only loader, orange only on new words and the Lounge's "new". Motion is fully specified (0.38 s rise, 0.28 s sink, 0.14 s out + 22 px, 0.3 s in after 0.1 s, 0.34 s cross-fade for intro/sharing/state changes, 0.98 press, 0.28 s answer hold, 0.16 s fades, reduce-motion instant). Engines: machine practise check (W1), signed line bank B01-B14 rotated never twice in a row with true-only 'later' lines (W2), communities with per-Take revocable consent stamped with the words' version, community clips first then own moments mixed with licensed-corpus training clips (CM1 A), switched on at once with the screen without waiting for counsel (CM2 B, against Claude's pick). NX1 A: this session builds the walk, nothing added, each screen shown in the panel's Done list with pictures before it goes live.

State today: only P1 exists (primitives, motion CSS, a dev-only harness at /dev/feedback-walk, signed copy files). Nothing live reads NEXT_PUBLIC_FEEDBACK_WALK; the speaker still gets the old DeckChunkModal/ParagraphSheet/PractiseSheet walk (judgement-first, speaker judges each practise). Backend W1 and W3 are built dark; W2 (line bank serving and rotation) is not started; the 3-try cap is not in the backend; COMMUNITY_SHARE_POLICY_VERSION=None still encodes the superseded 'wait for counsel' reading of CM2.

audits.tightness_why: Look, motion and every word are tight: the prototype gives exact sizes, colours, timings and easing, and every string is signed (N52.5, N54, N55). The flow is tight for one slide. Six gaps need a founder decision: (1) the order across several slides, because the prototype has one slide; (2) whether sharing is still asked after Skip on 'Judgement time!' (the prototype says yes, WQ1 A says the walk finishes); (3) where and how many other people's clips and training clips appear during judging (the lock says they do, the prototype draws none); (4) where a speaker takes sharing back for a past Take; (5) where the B10-B12 reason lines go, since the clearer-version screen has no place for them; (6) what the Exercise screen shows when there is no coach video. Which source wins: the lock file beats older design locks (lock preamble; frontend CLAUDE.md), and the later founder answers N53-N55 beat the lock file and the prototype where they are newer (CM3a cap, WQ1 Skip, WQ2 no 'coach is working' line, NX2 no photos, CM2 B switch on now).

questions.q: With several slides, in what order does the walk go?
questions.why: The prototype has one slide. The lock says 'all the praise, then the practising, then Judgement time!', but it doesn't say whether that covers the whole Take or one slide at a time. This decides the walk's order and the 'Slide 2 · moment 1 of 4' bar.
options: A: Whole Take. All praise from every slide, then all the practising, then one 'Judgement time!' for every moment. The bar shows each moment's own slide.
B: One slide at a time. Each slide's praise, then that slide's practising; one 'Judgement time!' at the end for all slides.
C: One slide at a time, each with its own praise, practising and judgements.
questions.recommended: A: it is the literal reading of the lock ('all the praise moments, then the moments to practise') and keeps one 'Judgement time!' per Take.

questions.q: If the speaker taps Skip on 'Judgement time!', do they still get the sharing question?
questions.why: WQ1 A says Skip 'finishes the walk' and clears the bars. The locked prototype's Skip goes to the sharing screen. Sharing is asked 'after every finished review'.
options: A: Yes. Skip goes to sharing, then the end card (as in the prototype).
B: No. Skip goes straight to the end card; this Take isn't shared unless asked another time.
questions.recommended: A: it keeps the locked screens unchanged and still asks the per-Take consent you called very important; the bars still clear as WQ1 A says.

questions.q: During judging, how many other people's clips and training clips does the speaker hear, and how are they shown?
questions.why: The lock says the community's Takes come first, then the speaker's own moments mixed with training clips. The prototype only shows the speaker's own moments. The server can serve up to 10 community clips and 3 training clips, which would make the walk much longer.
options: A: At most 3 other voices per walk, community clips first and training clips filling the rest, mixed among the speaker's own moments. Same judgement screen, without the slide bar.
B: Up to 3 community clips plus up to 3 training clips per walk.
C: No other voices inside the walk for now; judging others happens somewhere else later.
questions.recommended: A: it follows the lock's order without making the walk longer than the prototype, and adds no new words.

questions.q: Where does a speaker take back sharing for a Take they already shared?
questions.why: The consent must be withdrawable at any time, and the server already supports 'None'. But no locked screen opens the sharing question again for a past Take.
options: A: A 'Sharing' row in that Take's ⋯ menu opens the same locked sharing screen; 'None' takes it back.
B: A list of shared Takes on the Data & consent page, each with a switch.
C: Only the next time that Take's feedback is reviewed.
questions.recommended: A: it reuses the locked screen and its signed words. C would leave a consent with no way to withdraw it.

questions.q: Where do the clearer version's reason lines (B10 drop the word in front, B11 split in two, B12 join into one) appear?
questions.why: The bank is signed, but the locked clearer-version screen has only two lines: the opening (B13) and the question (B14). Neither the backend's 'repair the structure' rewrite nor 'join into one' has a clear match.
options: A: The reason line replaces the opening line (B13) when the rewrite has a clear reason; otherwise B13 shows. 'Repair the structure' rewrites show B12 only when sentences were joined, else B13.
B: The reason line goes under the new text, above the question (one new line on the locked screen).
C: B10-B12 are not shown to the speaker for now; only B13 and B14 rotate.
questions.recommended: A: no new element on the locked screen, and every line shown is a signed one.

questions.q: What does the Exercise screen show when the exercise has no coach video (a library exercise only)?
questions.why: The prototype draws 'the coach's video' and then 'Practise'. WQ2 B says the walk never says the coach is still working, so the moment waits silently. A library exercise matched by the machine may have its own video or none.
options: A: The library exercise's own video in the same frame; with no video at all, go straight to the practise screen.
B: The moment waits silently until a coach shares a video.
C: Always go straight to the practise screen with the instruction.
questions.recommended: A: the loop never waits for a coach (LIVE LOOP), and the screen stays exactly as drawn whenever a video exists.

questions.q: Before someone can share, which agreement version must they be on?
questions.why: CM2 B says sharing goes live with the screen, without waiting for counsel. The server still refuses every share until a policy version is named, and the message 'Please accept the updated Terms and Privacy first.' is signed. The current Privacy and Terms already contain 'Community sharing and peer review' sections.
options: A: The current version that already has the community sections (named in the code now); no new re-acceptance. Each share also records the version of the sharing screen's words.
B: Publish a new Terms/Privacy version that names communities, and ask everyone to accept it before the screen works.
questions.recommended: A: it is what CM2 B asked for (on at once, consent stamped with the words seen), and B would delay the feature.

questions.q: Should the word 'Journal' above the self-modeling post inside the walk be signed?
questions.why: The prototype shows a small 'Journal' label above the post. The code marks it as the one word on these screens that isn't signed yet.
options: A: Sign 'Journal' as shown.
B: No label; the post's title only.
questions.recommended: A: it is what the locked prototype shows.

audits.agreed_summary: The coach panel is redrawn in the Feedback walk's look and motion (full-screen overlay, grey profile picture, one player, same moves), one action per screen, choice cards shading white to darker grey with black text, "Something else" orange not bold. Flow: Lounge bubble "N speakers waiting · Open your queue" plus two pinned buttons with icons (Speakers = every speaker with an orange dot on those waiting; Training corpus) -> Your queue (your speakers only, moments waiting; below "Also waiting · blind": Do you hear it? and Pick the most confident moment, both described as built and switched off; corpus not in the queue) -> a speaker (Goal and Takes; tap a Take opens its first open moment; ‹ › between moments; counter counts moments only) -> Judge this moment (blind: player, question, five answers; no orange line; moves on by itself with "Answer saved") -> What happened (slide, passage with player, You / speaker / The machine heard) -> for errors the diagnosis first ("What kind of error is it?": machine-heard errors first marked "The machine heard this", then the others, "Something else · Name a new error", "I don't hear an error" which turns the answer into a note; Name the error is one field, the exercise reaches the speaker now and waits in the library under that name until a detector hears it) -> the cure ("Choose exercise": Keep it with Details, Swap it limited to exercises for the diagnosed error, Make a new one, Nothing to add; for praise, clearer version or note "What will you do?": Answer, Nothing to add; a choice moves on by itself, ‹ comes back to change it) -> Your words as the speaker will see them (speaker's passage and player on top, coach's words below with grey picture and a pencil) -> Your video (Record; an error without a video goes to the speaker without the library) -> kind question for praise and clearer version with Skip (shares without the library) -> Ready for {p} ("Share with {p}" or "Share without the library"; no "Keep it to this speaker") -> Summary for an answered moment ("Your answer", "Change my answer") -> A word for this Take (pencil, then its video step, Send). Training corpus (CO1 A): imports list, Import audio, set-up with the corpus page's own fields (topic, whose voice, language, source, what to run); an unfinished set-up opens before judging; moments judged blind on the same Judge screen. CP3 A: Library and Speaking errors leave the coach's app and go to the founder's admin area next to Pace. Speaker side: a paragraph without a bookmark does not open on tap. All CP2 words signed; N57 locks layout, flow and wording to the prototype; the new panel sits behind NEXT_PUBLIC_COACH_PANEL_V2 until the founder approves it screen by screen (P6); Judge stays blind and nothing about the moment is fetched until the coach's answer is saved. Precedence: the backend lock file wins over the FE CLAUDE.md section; the redesign lock wins over the October lock; the contract's 35g-2/35g-2a text is stale against the redesign and needs amending (it still says answers once, new exercises must name a detectable problem, and naming on the moment is retired).

audits.tightness_why: Layout, order, motion and nearly every word are pinned by the prototype copy and the CP2 list, so the screens themselves can be built without questions. The gaps are in what the screens must DO on the server: naming an error in one field collides with the construct rule and contract 35g-2; 'Change my answer' collides with the database's answer-once rule; a clearer version 'in the library' collides with C4; the error list for the diagnosis, the desktop layout, a handful of words the prototype draws but CP2 does not list, and the corpus page's extra controls are not decided. The build plan P2-P7 is not written down.

questions.q: When a coach names a new error in one field, where do its definition and its one question come from?
questions.why: The app's rule is that every error it keeps must have a written definition and one question (the backend refuses a name alone, speaking_error_library.py:68), and the contract says a new exercise must target an error the machine can hear. The locked screen has only the name.
options: A: Keep the one-field screen. The name is stored as a 'named by a coach' note, not yet a library error; you write its definition and question in your admin area before it becomes a real error. The exercise still reaches the speaker now and waits under that name.
B: Add two more fields (definition and question) to the coach's screen. Needs a new prototype and your signature.
C: The model drafts a definition and a question from the name; you sign them in admin.

questions.q: If a coach taps 'Change my answer' after the speaker already got the answer, what does the speaker see?
questions.why: Today an answer can never be changed (the database refuses), so the server must be changed, and someone has to decide what happens to the card the speaker already has.
options: A: The new answer replaces the old card on the speaker's moment; the old one stays only in history for audit.
B: A change is allowed only until the speaker has opened the card; after that, Change my answer is not shown.
C: Both stay: the speaker sees the newer answer marked as updated by the coach.

questions.q: Should a coach's clearer version go into the library when they pick 'What kind of fix is it?'
questions.why: Your September answer (C4) and the contract say a clearer version never goes to the library because it is one speaker's own words. The new prototype's share screen says 'in the library' after the kind question.
options: A: Never. The kind is recorded only to label the coach's work; the screen shows 'Share with {p}' alone, as it does for a note.
B: Only the kind of fix is filed (no speaker words), so the library learns which fixes coaches use.
C: The clearer version itself is filed and can be offered to other speakers.

questions.q: Which errors are listed under 'the others' on 'What kind of error is it?'
questions.why: The lock says the errors the machine heard come first, then the others, but not which others.
options: A: Every active error in the library: the ones the machine hears, the ones being tested, and the ones coaches named, so coaches converge on the same names.
B: Only errors the machine can hear or is testing; coach-named ones only via 'Something else'.
C: Only the errors the machine can hear today.

questions.q: What does 'every coach who names it brings that closer' mean in practice?
questions.why: Since 5 Oct (N48.5 Q24 A) an error becomes ready for a detector only through coaches' blind 'Do you hear it?' answers, and naming on the moment was retired (N45 Q9). A diagnosis is given after the coach saw the machine's read, so it is not blind.
options: A: Naming is counted and shown to you on the admin errors page as a signal for which detector to build next; readiness still comes only from the blind check.
B: Naming also counts toward readiness, next to the blind answers.

questions.q: How should the new coach panel look on a computer screen?
questions.why: In September you chose a side rail on desktop (B10). The new prototype is drawn for a phone only, and the lock says nothing may be added that it does not show.
options: A: The same phone-width screens, centred, no rail (like the speaker's Feedback walk).
B: Keep the September rail (speakers, Takes, moment states as words) beside the centred screens; needs a desktop prototype for your signature.

questions.q: A few words appear on the locked prototype but are not on the CP2 list. Are they signed with the design?
questions.why: The build may only use signed words. Examples: 'All answered · 3 Takes' on Speakers, 'Camera' and 'Recording' on the video screens, 'Kept: …', 'Swapped: …', 'Shared · in the library' on Summary, 'Back in the library' in admin. Also CP2 signed 'Choose a file' while the prototype shows 'Choose files', and signed '{n} imports', '{n} moments to judge', 'One recording · it is cut into moments you judge blind' have no place on any locked screen.
options: A: Yes, everything the prototype shows is signed with the design lock (N57); where CP2 and the prototype differ, CP2's words win ('Choose a file'); signed words with no place are not used.
B: Send me the list on one screen to sign word by word before those screens are built.

questions.q: 'Do you hear it?' is switched on in the backend today, though the lock says it is off. Should it show in the new queue?
questions.why: It was switched on on 2 Oct (N26) and is now the only way an error becomes ready for a detector; the 6 Oct lock describes it as off.
options: A: Keep it on; it shows under 'Also waiting · blind' whenever there is one.
B: Switch it off until you say so.

questions.q: Is a coach's note shared straight from 'Ready for {p}' with no library question (the old D4)?
questions.why: D4 was parked until this prototype existed; the prototype shows a note going straight to 'Ready for {p}' with one button, and lists D4 under 'Still to decide'.
options: A: Yes, as drawn: no library question for a note, the last button reads 'Share with {p}'.
B: Add a library question for notes too (needs new words to sign).

questions.q: The training corpus page today can hide, delete and restore imports. The locked screens show none of that. Keep those controls?
questions.why: The lock forbids elements the prototype does not show, but deleting a bad import is sometimes needed.
options: A: Drop them from the coach's screens; deleting or restoring an import moves to your admin area.
B: Drop them entirely.
C: Keep them on the coach's screens (needs a prototype change you sign).

questions.q: When is the training corpus import switched on for coaches?
questions.why: The machine side and your legal basis (N58) are in place, but the import switch is still off in code, and the coach-facing screens are not yet the locked ones.
options: A: Together with the new panel's corpus screens, after you approve their pictures.
B: Now, on today's corpus page, and move to the new screens later.

audits.agreed_summary: Locked 2026-10-07 (N59, prototype v7). Take 1 opens on a learning screen with no slide, clock or Finish take: on a phone "Scroll down to start" over a nudging chevron, on a desktop four arrow keys (down lit) over "Click down to start". A swipe, scroll, Down, Page Down, Space or Enter starts the recording and the slide glides in. A later Take goes straight from "Record Take N" to "Getting your mic ready" and starts by itself, with no Start-recording screen (the optional training question may still come first). The recording screen has "Take N · Slide n of m" on the left of the top bar (no "Recording" label) and the close button on the right. The slide sits close under the bar (about 20px). Below it are the speaker's helper words, all orange, with none on Take 1. The slide dots are on the right. The bottom strip holds the dot, clock, bar and "Finish take", with no line above it. Motion: only the slide and its helper words move, under a still top bar, dots and strip. The content follows the finger and a slide moves after 90px. On wheel or trackpad it moves at 140, or at 90 followed by a 220ms rest, and the 450ms momentum tail is ignored. A move goes out in 200ms and lands in 420ms on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), and is instant with reduce motion. The helper words scroll before the slide moves. Keys work without a click first. Pulling or scrolling at the top never reloads the page. "Discard this take?" and the processing wait stay as they are today; after the wait comes the Ideal Text page. Precedence: this lock wins over the Ideal Text lock's Recording Mode line. The lock file wins over the frontend CLAUDE.md. The walk lock's 0.4s fade for entering Recording Mode is not contradicted, because the recording prototype does not draw that move, but its "dark" conflicts with the white screens. Verdict: the build in #630/#631 matches the flow, words, gesture numbers and keys. Six visible differences remain: the close X style, the loader label being screen-reader only, a 24px top-padding difference on the learning screen and mic loader, a 32px instead of 20px bottom gap under the strip, a no-pull-to-refresh hole on the later-Take mic screen, and the unbuilt 0.4s fade into Recording Mode. There is also no committed browser test of the lock. FILTER: ADVANCE-F1-SURFACE - cat F1-SURFACE (record->Take) - fences clear - locks clear - redirect: none.

audits.tightness_why: The flow, the new words, and every gesture number, curve and key are written as numbers in the lock and the prototype, and the build matches them. A builder could reproduce those with no questions. Four small gaps remain. The close X is drawn differently in every locked prototype while the app has one shared X. 'Getting your mic ready' is a visible label in the prototype but screen-reader only in the app, and the lock also says 'every other word is today's'. The walk lock's 0.4s 'fades to dark' entrance clashes with the white recording screens. The real microphone-permission moment before the Take 1 learning screen is not drawn. The 24px/20px spacing differences need no decision, because the lock says the prototype wins.

questions.q: The close button (X) at the top right of the recording screen: the prototype draws a bigger plain dark X, the app uses its usual small grey X in a thin circle, and each locked design draws it a little differently. Which X should the recording screens use?
questions.why: The recording lock says to build exactly as the prototype shows. The Feedback-walk lock says one look everywhere. The coach-panel, consent and recording prototypes each draw a different X, so the two locks pull in opposite directions.
options: A. Keep the app's one X everywhere (small grey X in a thin circle). Note in the lock that the prototypes only approximated it.
B. Use the prototype's bigger plain X on the recording screens only.
C. Switch the whole app to the recording prototype's bigger plain X.
questions.recommended: A. One X across the app keeps the 'one look everywhere' rule, and the difference is a few pixels. The decisions log records it, so nobody 'fixes' it later.

questions.q: On the 'Getting your mic ready' screen, should the words show under the breathing mark, as in the prototype? Today the app shows only the mark and the words are read out only by screen readers.
questions.why: The prototype draws the words in small grey text, while the lock also says 'every other word on these screens is today's', and today they are invisible. A builder cannot tell which you meant.
options: A. Show 'Getting your mic ready' in small grey text under the mark, exactly as the prototype draws it.
B. Keep the mark only (words for screen readers), as today.
questions.recommended: A. The lock names the screen by those words, and the prototype is the reference for every screen.

questions.q: Moving from your text into a recording, and back: the Feedback-walk design says Recording Mode 'fades to dark' in 0.4 seconds, but the locked recording screens are white. What should the move look like? Today it is instant.
questions.why: The walk lock asks for a 0.4s fade, but its 'dark' is a stand-in screen that the newer recording lock replaced with white screens. The move has not been built.
options: A. A soft 0.4-second fade into the white recording screens and back out (no dark).
B. Fade through black for 0.4 seconds, then the white recording screen.
C. Keep it instant, as today.
questions.recommended: A. It keeps the walk lock's timing and the recording lock's look. No new element or word is added.

questions.q: On the first recording, the phone or browser has to ask permission to use the microphone before the 'Scroll down to start' screen can work. The prototype goes straight to that screen. What should the speaker see while the permission question is up?
questions.why: A real browser needs the microphone to open first. The prototype cannot show that moment, so today the app briefly shows the breathing mark first.
options: A. Keep the breathing mark for that moment, then 'Scroll down to start' appears (today).
B. Show 'Scroll down to start' at once. If the speaker scrolls before the microphone is ready, the recording begins as soon as it is.
questions.recommended: A. Nothing on the screen promises a start that cannot happen yet, and the wait is usually under a second.

audits.agreed_summary:
Agreed (N60, founder 2026-10-07, prototype TuMKSE2BH364ZQ1Eq4UMdd v2): the first-time walk (welcome "Enter the lab" with no top bar; agreement notice with three documents, each marked "read ✓"; each document's own screen with "Done reading" and "Back"; "Where do you live?"; "Three things to confirm", with the age tick, the sensitive-information tick and an Optional "Personalised practice" tick, then "Agree and continue" or "Do not agree"; "Nothing was recorded"). Also the Data & consent page, and "Turn on the learning?" before every Take while training is off. Skip is not remembered; Yes is never asked again. Every step scrolls from its true top on any phone. A document's title and buttons stay still and only its text scrolls. Today's words are kept, except "Two" becomes "Three things to confirm". Legal text always comes from the active policy. The prototype's stand-ins (dashed boxes, project names, country list, pop-up notes, Learning chip) are not locked.

ST1 A amendment (prototype 4jDJsvBAquMUgaGkJgHR76): the ☰ menu has no Support and no Community row. The current page's row stays orange on light orange. A Support card sits between Your projects and Delete my account: the title, the address contact@willpowerlab.com shown as selectable text, and a small round copy button. Privacy and Terms opened from Data & consent show "Back" and return there, to the same scroll position. Opened from elsewhere they keep "Back home". "Support" and "Back" are signed.

Precedence: where frontend CLAUDE.md and the backend lock file disagree, the lock file wins. Here they agree. The prototype is the reference for layout, flow, motion and words.

Two live bugs.
- Training "Turn on": the fix is migration 0436 (C1 accepts a receipt held by the account or by the principal it resolves to). It shipped in backend #921, which GitHub shows merged 2026-10-07 15:38Z, so with MIGRATE_ON_BOOT it ran on the next deploy. It is not yet verified in prod.
- "Your projects" empty: the only fix so far is the loader in #633. The root cause is unproven. The most likely cause is a slow /v2/user/trainings: one extra coach-edits query per project with slides, while the pre-#633 card rendered nothing during the load. A silent [] on a database error is the second candidate.

FILTER: JUSTIFIED-SCAFFOLDING. Category: F1-SURFACE for the acceptance/processing boundary in front of the live loop, SCAFFOLDING for the settings page. Fences clear: no new words without sign-off; LIVE LOOP needs agreement and recording to stay reachable. Locks clear.

audits.tightness_why: Both prototypes are exact HTML/CSS with every live word, so layout, spacing, words and the main flows can be built without questions, and almost all of them are. Four gaps remain. The prototypes never draw error or empty states: an empty project list, failed loads, a refused training yes. They do not draw the conditional 'What's changed since you agreed' card. They do not draw the built-but-dark project deletion. Whether the support address should stay a mail link is ambiguous: the founder said 'just an email', while the prototype shows plain text with a copy button. Motion and scroll-reset are specified only implicitly, through the prototype's render() code and its .enter animation, not in the lock text.

questions.q: Deleting a single project is already built but switched off, and the settings page you locked shows no Delete next to projects. What should happen to it?
questions.why: Turning it on would add buttons and words the locked page does not have. Leaving it ambiguous risks someone switching it on later and breaking the lock.
options: A: Keep it switched off. It goes live only after you see and sign a clickable version of the settings page that includes it.
B: Remove the switched-off project-delete code entirely; people delete projects only by deleting their whole account.
C: Switch it on now as built (it would change the locked page: 'Delete a project' button and a Delete on each row).

questions.q: If someone really has no projects yet, what should 'Your projects' show when they open it?
questions.why: Today it shows only the heading with nothing under it, which is exactly what looked like a bug to you. The locked page doesn't draw this case, and any new sentence needs your sign-off.
options: A: Leave it as it is: just the heading.
B: Add one short line you sign, for example 'No projects yet.'
C: Hide the 'Your projects' button until the person has a project.

questions.q: The card 'What’s changed since you agreed' (you signed it on 28 September) appears on Data & consent only when the terms changed after someone agreed. The locked settings page doesn't draw it. Keep it?
questions.why: The lock says nothing may appear that the prototype doesn't show. This card is older than the lock and is how a person accepts updated terms from settings.
options: A: Keep it as signed; it only shows when terms changed.
B: First add it to the settings prototype so you can see and lock how it looks, then keep it.

questions.q: On the Support card, should tapping the address open the person's email app?
questions.why: Today the address is an underlined link that opens the mail app. Your locked prototype shows plain text you can select, plus a small copy button. Building exactly to the prototype removes the link.
options: A: Exactly as the prototype: plain text plus the copy button, no mail link.
B: Both: the copy button, and the address still opens the mail app (looks the same as the prototype, without the underline).
C: Keep the mail link and skip the copy button.

questions.q: If 'Turn on' for Help improve WillpowerLab still fails because the person first has to accept updated terms, what should they see?
questions.why: Today every refusal says 'Couldn’t save that. Try again.', and in this case trying again can never work. The fix shipped today should remove the common case, but not this one.
options: A: Keep today's words, but record the real reason for us so we can fix it fast.
B: Show the existing 'What’s changed since you agreed' card with its 'Accept the update' button instead, then let them turn it on.
C: Write a new sentence for this case (needs your sign-off).

audits.agreed_summary:
FILTER: ADVANCE-F1 for the audit's redirect work (cat F1-CORE: transcription, bucketing, Paragraph identity, Manager arbitration) — fences clear (all V4 measures internal, AC-9; coach screens blind) — locks clear — redirect: (1) measure bucketing and transcript fidelity, which nobody measures today; (4) make the rewrite lane actually fill.

WHAT IS AGREED
1. Transcription and slides. One transcription call over the whole recording returns word times. Each word goes to the slide that was on screen when it was spoken, corrected by the measured offset between the phone's clock and the audio. A deck recording with no slide taps belongs to the slide it started on (contract 8, N29.3, N33.1). A revisited slide joins its slide (N31). A document whose slides cannot be proven follows the Take whole (N33.2).
2. Ideal Text. Take 1's Ideal Text is the speaker's own words with only minimal smoothing. Each later Take rewrites every slide it spoke. A slide not spoken keeps the speaker's current words, owner edits included (contract 8 as amended by N29 and N48.1). A Paragraph keeps its ID through rewording, proven by count (contract 12, lock B1). V4 matches a Paragraph by its place on the slide, with the slide as backup (V10b A).
3. V3 is served to every speaker (contract 24, N29.1, N32). Each slide run is cut into blocks of about 75 words (normally 60-90) at piece boundaries, never crossing a slide (24a). Each valid block gets exactly one relative-best Confident Voice item on every Take (24b). Within a block, what the words did is ranked before how they sounded (24j, behind a switch). Notes are anchored by the machine's read, one per block: praise where the read is confident, a clearer version where it is weak, and an exercise on any weak bookmark the library matches (24f, caps lifted). An honest empty lane shows no card (25). Coverage is 70/80/100% of the slides that formed at least one block, as a target and never a floor (24c/24d). At most three open items show at a time (24b window). V3 fails visibly, retries once, and never falls back to V2 (24h, N32).
4. V4 (V4 decision page, N51; contract 24 and 24h as amended 2026-10-06). V4 is a new picker. Its sound read decides which kinds of note a moment may carry (M2/P1). It ranks moments by importance × (1 − S·W) × sureness (P2):
   - importance: one batched AI call per Take tags each moment's role from a fixed list (O1, V13 A).
   - S·W: willfidence-v1, the sound score times the words score (SPEC §17).
   - sureness: evidence strength × (1 − disagreement between the sound reads) (QB6 A).
   Confident Voice stays on the best-sounding moment of each block (P3). V4 picks the moment and the kind of note; the exercise picker picks the video (V16a A). A block V4 is very unsure of gets V3's pick, and the fallback is logged (V15 A). Falling back on more than 1 block in 5 fails the exit gate (V15a A).
   - The switch: no dark run; a few speakers first, then everyone (V22a B). V4 runs alone, with no hidden V3 beside it for comparison (V22c B). There is no estimate from past data (QG7 A).
   - Phase 1 measures first: 1.1 pick logging for every speaker (V1 A); 1.2 a seeded random 20% of moments (V2 A, V3 A); 1.3 willfidence read by the machine (V4 A, V5 B, V6 A, QG8 A); 1.4 a fast read of each practice try, p90 at most 5 s (O5, V7 A); 1.4b the reached bar (O4, V8 A, V9 A); 1.5 whether the picked paragraph rose by the next Take (V10b A, V11 B, V12 A, QG2a A); 1.7 vote counts (V17 A); 1.8 the coach sheet "Pick the moment for feedback" (QB7 A, QB7a B, QG4 B, QG9 A, QG5 A); 1.9 "Which sounds surer" (V19 A, V20 A, QB8 A).
   - Exit gate: any margin, at least 100 golden blocks (V21 A).
   - Learned models (recognizer, picker, feedback writer; M1/M5) and training stay parked (M10, P-b).
5. Precedence. The contract states that it wins over older text. The N51 amendments (24, 24h) replace "V3 is the served policy". The Feedback-walk lock (2026-10-06) wins over older design locks. Coach-panel lock L6 narrows V4's M9 and V18: the golden set is the founder's picks alone. SPEC §17 still says willfidence is "never a ranking term", which clashes with V4's P2; under the CONSTRUCT fence the stricter text holds until the founder decides (Q3).

audits.tightness_why: V3 is tightly specified and almost entirely built. The gaps are measurement (transcript and bucketing accuracy, coverage persistence) and three engineering defects: the rewrite lane rarely fills, an accepted rewrite does not re-anchor, and the no_defensible_candidate outcome is not stored. A builder could do these without questions, apart from the rule for AI-written rewrites. V4 is loose. O1 (role list) and O3 (WORDS definitions) are open, and O3 blocks W under the CONSTRUCT fence. O2 (the cut-off) was to be set from dark-run data, but V22a B removed the dark run. The exit gate still says 'beats V3' after V22c B removed the comparison. SPEC §17 says willfidence is 'never a ranking term' while V4's P2 ranks by it. What V4 changes on the page (V16a vs P3 and the window rule) is unstated, the 'clear rise' margin (V11 B) has no number, and the practice-try rule differs between the Feedback-walk lock (better than before) and V4's 2.2 (reached the bar). Phase 1 items 1.2, 1.4b and 1.7 are tight enough to build now.

questions.q: There is no longer a trial run of V4 next to V3. What must V4 show before it stays on for everyone?
questions.why: The exit gate says 'V4 beats V3', but you chose to skip the trial run (V22a B) and to run V4 alone (V22c B). As written, the gate cannot be checked, and 100 golden blocks at about 10 a week takes about 10 weeks.
options: A: V4 goes to a few speakers, then everyone. The check runs afterwards: it falls back on no more than 1 block in 5, slide coverage holds, and practice reads are fast. 'Beats V3' is dropped.
B: As A, and on your own golden blocks only, V3's pick is worked out again for comparison (it is never shown to anyone). If V4 does worse there, you decide whether to switch back.
C: Keep a one-week hidden trial on your own Takes only, then a few speakers, then everyone.
questions.recommended: B: V3's pick for each block is already computed for the fallback, so comparing on your golden blocks costs nothing and needs no hidden V3 beside V4 for speakers.

questions.q: How unsure must V4 be before a block falls back to V3's pick?
questions.why: You chose to set this from trial-run data (V14 A), but the trial run is gone (V22a B). Without a number, V4 cannot be built.
options: A: Start with a level where about 1 block in 10 falls back, then reset it from the first 100 V4 Takes. A versioned number, never shown.
B: Fall back only when V4 has no evidence at all for a block.
C: Run V4 hidden on your own Takes for one week and pick the level from that.
questions.recommended: A: it stays well inside your 'more than 1 in 5 fails' limit (V15a) and learns from real Takes without a trial run.

questions.q: Can V4 use the words half of willfidence to choose feedback before every word quality is written down?
questions.why: V4 ranks by sound × words (P2). The written definition in SPEC §17 says willfidence is 'never a ranking term' and that no word quality is measured until it has a written definition (O3 open). Under the construct fence V4 cannot ship as decided until this is settled.
options: A: Claude writes one-sentence definitions for the four word qualities measured today (filler rate, hedging, slide alignment, staying on topic) for your signature. Naturalness waits, and SPEC §17 is amended to allow ranking in V4.
B: V4 ranks by sound only until all five word qualities are defined.
C: V4 waits until all five are defined.
questions.recommended: A: the four exist in code today, and one sentence each is all the fence needs.

questions.q: What does V4 change on the speaker's page compared with V3?
questions.why: V16a says V4 'picks moment and kind'. P3 and contract 24b say each block's bookmark stays on its best-sounding moment, and the window-of-three rule already decides which three show. Without an answer the builder must guess.
options: A: V4 decides which three open moments show first and which note (praise, clearer version or exercise) each carries. Each block keeps its best-sounding bookmark, and 'never three of one colour' stays.
B: V4 also chooses which moment inside a block becomes the bookmark, replacing 'best-sounding'.
C: V4 only chooses the kind of note; the window rule is unchanged.
questions.recommended: A: it uses V4's ranking where it adds value without touching the per-block rule (24b) or the coverage targets.

questions.q: After a practice try, which rule decides 'praise' vs 'try again'?
questions.why: The Feedback-walk lock has the machine check whether the try is better than the original (built, switched off). V4's walk (2.2) instead praises when the try reaches a set bar. The two can disagree on the same try.
options: A: Keep 'better than before' now. Move to 'reached the bar' only once the bar is calibrated and you sign the new walk.
B: Praise when either rule says yes.
C: Switch to the bar now using the stand-in 0.6.
questions.recommended: A: the walk lock is the newer signed rule, and the bar does not exist yet.

questions.q: May an AI-written clearer version reach the speaker?
questions.why: Today only one narrow rule and a tentative fallback produce clearer versions; every AI-written one is blocked because it carries no evidence. Most weak moments get no clearer version, against 24f's 'a rewrite on every item read weak'.
options: A: Yes, when its quoted words are exactly the speaker's and a detector found a problem in those words (fillers, hedging, run-on), worded tentatively when the evidence is weak.
B: No. Keep only rule-made clearer versions.
C: Yes, always, but always worded tentatively.
questions.recommended: A: it fills the lane with evidence behind every card, so nothing is invented (L2, contract 25).

questions.q: Should each block's bookmark go first to moments whose words made their point, then to the best-sounding one?
questions.why: You agreed this rule on 23 September (24j). It is built but switched off. The V4 page (P3) says 'best-sounding moment'.
options: A: Turn it on now, on every service at once (words first, then sound).
B: Keep it off: best-sounding only, as V4's P3 says.
C: Leave it off until V4 is built, then decide.
questions.recommended: A: it is signed and built, and V4's words term points the same way. It must be switched on together on web, worker and background jobs.

questions.q: How do we prove the transcript is right and the words land on the right slide?
questions.why: Nothing measures either today. 'Perfect transcript' and 'exactly 1:1 per slide' are the first two F1 pieces, and the old way of catching slide errors (coach corrections) was removed.
options: A: You record about 10 scripted Takes, read from a known text with the slide taps logged, some with an accent or background noise. These become a fixed test set.
B: Use speakers' own text edits as a rough, internal-only error count.
C: Both.
questions.recommended: C: A gives a true score, and B shows drift on real Takes between the scripted checks.

questions.q: Who sets the size of a 'clear rise' when V4 checks whether a picked paragraph got better?
questions.why: You chose 'only a clear rise' (V11 B), but no number exists. It decides what V4 learns from and what the exit check reads.
options: A: Claude proposes a number with reasons on one panel screen, versioned, for your signature.
B: You set it now.
C: Any rise counts.

audits.agreed_summary: What is agreed, in plain words. (1) Four learning doors, each a code constant flipped only by a reviewed change that carries the founder's sentence (LEARNING-DOORS.md). Door 1 (the speaker's training yes) is open since 2026-10-01 (N15) and was fixed for claimed guest accounts by 0436 (N61). Door 2 (weekly signed release of coach-answer pairs) is open in code for praise_line, clearer_version and exercise_script (N16, N18). The two coach-word surfaces stay shut until a lawyer answers (N18, N23 Q8). Door 3 (fine-tune at 200 pairs with a sealed founder golden set of 50 judgements per surface, ML-10/ML-11, L6, QG4 B) and door 4 (promotion after a passing golden evaluation with the regurgitation check, ML-12) are built and closed. A pair trains once (P53 A), and pairs from before 6 October stay out (QA16 B). (2) The training corpus (N56.4 CO1 A): coaches import audio the founder holds the rights to. Each import gets the same V3 moment spotting a Take gets, with the machine's pick stored and never shown, and a fixed 80/20 learn/test split by speaker. Imports run under one founder corpus basis, with no per-import licence (N58 CO2, 0435). An importer's blind label counts like any coach's (CO3 A). Nothing trains on any of it until the founder says so. The corpus screens are locked to the coach-panel prototype: a pinned Lounge button, the list, Import audio, a set-up step that must finish before judging, the app's one loader, and blind judging on the same Judge screen, with the CP2-signed words. (3) The label ledger: the machine routes and never votes. Quorum is two blind humans, never the speaker. One answer alone is never gold (J1-J5, K1-K12). (4) The W8 confidence chain is connected (N48.5 Q27 A): one consent authority (the training yes), and the coach walk's blind labels become its judgements. Training stays closed, the confidence read stays rule-based until the SPEC evaluation passes (L9), and the chain reaches whoever the founder puts in the confidence_learning_writes ring. (5) Voice Album: Machine Yes (today's V3 sound read, QG13 A) plus User Yes plus Coach Yes, all on the exact same recording (contract 32). The welcome shows as soon as the first moment enters (QB18a A). (6) Founder-only pages: the pace panel jars (C9, ML-4) and the research screen (ML-7). Coach-work numbers are added to the pace panel (QA20 A). (7) Clean-up: remove the audio-copying training-corpus copy job, keeping its table (QB4 A). The founder runs one prepared script that switches the training_corpus retention rule off (QB3 A). Keep the readiness alarm and find why it fails (R4a A). Reword the audit questions so that low volume and flat pitch can be promoted (QA14 A). What is live today: door 1, door 2 in code, golden-set judging, the weekly job code, the pace and research pages, Voice Album capture, the W8 chain for ring-5 speakers only, and the blind error audit. What is dark: corpus imports (TRAINING_IMPORT_ENABLED=False), doors 3 and 4, detector training, learned exercise order, the peer lane, communities and the coach-word surfaces. What blocks real learning today: (a) the corpus switch is off, so no corpus labels exist; (b) door 2 sends nothing out until PAIR_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY and the weekly cron service are confirmed on Railway (A087b, A101, A082); (c) door 3 waits for the founder's 50 golden judgements per surface and for 200 exportable pairs; (d) the W8 chain reaches ring 5 only, which in practice means the founder, and the founder's own training yes failed until 0436; (e) nothing exists yet that turns settled sound labels into an evaluation or a model (A109c open; L9 names an evaluation but no build); (f) only coaches can settle a quorum while the peer lane and communities are dark.

audits.tightness_why: Tight: the doors and their exact conditions; the golden set (50, sealed, founder alone); quorum rules J/K; the Album's three legs; the N58 basis; CO3; and the clean-up decisions (QB3, QB4, QB18a). A builder can do each without a question. Small gaps: the corpus screens. The CP2 signed list and the locked prototype disagree ('Choose a file' vs 'Choose files'; signed strings the prototype never shows; prototype strings that were never signed). The prototype's 'set-up not finished' state has no backend meaning yet (does finishing set-up re-run the transcription in the chosen language?). Under the frontend CLAUDE.md, the lock file wins over the prototype where they disagree, but neither covers the strings that only one of them shows. Loose: the end state of sound-confidence learning. L9 says the read stays rules until 'the SPEC's evaluation' passes, but no metric, threshold or build is agreed (ledger A109c). Corpus labels (confidence_labels, 80/20 by label) and Take judgements (ml_judgments, 80/10/10 by bound speaker) live in two stores with two split schemes, and nothing decides how they meet. Who the W8 chain reaches is undecided beyond 'the founder's panel act'.

questions.q: The training corpus: should coaches be able to import audio now? You answered 'switch it on' (CO1 A), but the code shipped with the switch still off.
questions.why: TRAINING_IMPORT_ENABLED is False (config.py:288), so no corpus audio can be imported or judged and no corpus labels exist. Everything behind the switch is built and tested, including your legal basis (N58).
options: A: Turn it on now. Coaches import on today's corpus page, and the locked corpus screens replace it later behind the coach-panel switch.
B: Wait until the locked corpus screens are built and you have approved them screen by screen.
C: Keep it off for now.
questions.recommended: A. Nothing reaches a speaker, judging is blind on either page, and the labels start to build up while the screens are made.

questions.q: Whose real Takes should feed the confidence-learning chain? Today it reaches only people on ring 5, which in practice means you.
questions.why: The chain is connected (Q27 A), but the ring row confidence_learning_writes is set to ring 5 (0430: 'moving it is the founder's panel act'). No other speaker's blind coach judgement enters it.
options: A: Everyone who has said yes to training, once the readiness alarm reads green.
B: A small named group first (you move them to ring 5), then everyone.
C: Only you until training opens.
questions.recommended: A, after the alarm is green. Only people who said yes enter, the Take never waits on the chain (N27), and there are no other users to protect yet.

questions.q: What should the coaches' blind confidence answers (corpus and Takes) be used for before any training is allowed?
questions.why: L9 says the confidence read stays rule-based until an evaluation passes, but nothing compares the machine's read with what two coaches heard, and no trainer exists (ledger A109c).
options: A: Only to measure how often today's machine read agrees with two coaches, on your research screen, never shown to coaches or speakers.
B: A, plus build the confidence trainer now, switched off until you say 'open door 3' for it.
C: Nothing yet. Collect until about 100 settled clips, then decide.
questions.recommended: A. It is the evaluation L9 already asks for, it trains nothing, and it tells you when B is worth building.

questions.q: The corpus screens' words: your signed list (CP2) and the locked prototype disagree. Which do we build?
questions.why: The prototype shows 'Choose files', 'No speaker label', 'All {n} labelled' and 'Analysing on the server…', which are not on the signed list. The signed list has 'Choose a file', '{n} imports · {n} moments to judge' and 'One recording · it is cut into moments you judge blind', which the prototype never shows. The lock file wins on a clash, but neither source settles the strings only one of them has.
options: A: Build the prototype as drawn, with the signed 'Choose a file' in place of 'Choose files', and you sign the four prototype-only lines.
B: Build only signed words: leave out the four prototype-only lines and place the extra signed lines where the builder sees fit.
C: You redraw the corpus screens in the prototype first.
questions.recommended: A. It keeps the picture you locked and changes one word to the one you signed.

questions.q: How should the blind error audit ask about low volume and flat pitch, so that a Yes means the problem is there?
questions.why: You chose to reword them (QA14 A), but the words need your signature. Until then these two cues can never be promoted (ledger A092, A072b).
options: A: 'Is the voice too quiet here?' and 'Does the voice stay on one note here?'
B: 'Is it hard to hear the speaker here?' and 'Does the voice sound flat here?'
C: Leave both out of the audit for now.
questions.recommended: A. Each asks one thing, a Yes means the problem is there, and both match how the machine measures it.

questions.q: The coach-work block on your pace panel (QA20 A): which labels should it show?
questions.why: The numbers are already computed. The ledger says the labels need your sign-off before the block can be drawn.
options: A: 'Coach requests per opened moment' with one row per kind: exercise, praise, clearer version, note.
B: The same numbers with no title, kinds only.
C: Not now.

questions.q: Speakers will now be sent to the Voice Album page as soon as their first moment enters, but that page has no locked design. Lock it?
questions.why: Every other speaker screen is built inch-perfect to a locked prototype. The album page (src/app/voice-album) predates the locks, and the welcome bubble points to it.
options: A: We show you screenshots of today's page; if you approve, it is locked as is.
B: The design session draws the album page first, and the welcome waits for it.
C: Ship the welcome now and decide the page later.
questions.recommended: A. It is the quickest way to bring the page under a lock without holding back the welcome you asked for.
