audits.tightness_why: Most items are tied to a specific decision, a signed artifact hash, a script and a constant, so a builder could finish v1.4/03 registration, the boot-line change, the switch flips and the Terms 3.4 draft without asking anything. Five points need the founder. (1) N55 removes a consent that two screens locked a day later (N60) still show, and it also removes the blind check's only off switch (counsel question 10). (2) CM2 B says go live with sharing without counsel, but the code ties a share to a published policy version and Privacy 3.3 does not mention communities. (3) Project Delete is agreed (Q17 A, S1 A), but the locked settings page has no Delete. (4) Which older audio stores fall under the 12-month rule (A210b) is open. (5) The cleaner's first real run is explicitly the founder's word. Where sources conflict, the lock files' own rule applies: the later lock wins for screens until the founder approves a prototype of the change, and the decisions log wins over stale code comments.

questions.q: Once practise is part of the service, how can a speaker still stop the 'blind check' (a coach listening to a short anonymous clip of them to check our software), which today they stop by switching off practice?
questions.why: Privacy 3.3 lines 99-102 make the Personalised practice switch the only way to object to the blind check. N55 removes that switch, so something must replace it before the change can be published. Counsel question 10 asks the same thing. Any new switch would sit on a locked screen.
options: A: Add a small separate switch on Data & consent, 'Don't use my clips for checks' (needs a clickable prototype for your approval, because the screen is locked)
B: No switch. Privacy says 'email us to object', and we mark that person by hand so the check never picks their clips
C: Stop using speakers' Takes for the blind check and use only the imported training corpus
questions.recommended: B while counsel answers question 10. If counsel says it must be self-service, move to A.

questions.q: Should the legal text changes ship as one new version of the Privacy Policy and Terms, or in two steps?
questions.why: Four changes are waiting: packages bought once (Terms §2, counsel question 11), the Privacy §4b reword (QB21 A), a line about community sharing, and practise as part of the service (N55, which must wait for counsel). Every new version means every user accepts again.
options: A: Version 3.4 now with packages, §4b and the sharing line, signed by you. Practise-as-service follows later as 3.5, after counsel
B: Wait and put everything into one version after counsel has answered
C: Publish only the packages text now and leave the rest

questions.q: When community sharing goes live with the walk, what record does each 'yes, share this Take' point to?
questions.why: You decided sharing goes live without waiting for counsel (CM2 B). The code will only accept a share from someone who accepted a Privacy version that mentions sharing, and today's Privacy 3.3 does not mention communities, so with nothing set every share is refused.
options: A: Add a one-paragraph sharing line to Privacy 3.4 (see the previous question). Each share records 3.4 plus the signed sharing words
B: Go live with only the per-Take sharing screen and record the date of its signed words. Update Privacy later
C: Keep sharing off until counsel has read the words

questions.q: When should the automatic clean-up start really deleting old recordings (12 months unused), unclaimed guest accounts (30 days) and old technical logs (90 days)?
questions.why: It is built and today only counts. Your report of 5 October found nothing due, so switching it on deletes nothing today but keeps the promises in the retention schedule automatically from now on.
options: A: Let it count every night for one week, you glance at the counts, then switch it on
B: Keep it counting only, and switch it on when the count first shows something due
C: Switch it on now

questions.q: Some older parts of the app keep audio that the clean-up does not see. What should happen to it?
questions.why: The 12-month rule today covers only the main recordings store (ledger A210b). Audio kept elsewhere would stay forever, which the retention schedule does not allow.
options: A: First get a one-page list of every place audio is kept, then bring each one under the 12-month rule
B: If those places are no longer written to, delete their old audio once, after a preview you approve
C: Leave it, and say so in the next retention schedule
questions.recommended: A, with B for any place that turns out to be retired

questions.q: Should speakers be able to delete a single project from the settings page?
questions.why: You agreed this (Q17 A), switched on once deletions can actually finish. But the settings page you locked on 7 October shows projects with Archive only, and the lock forbids adding a button without your approval of a prototype. Account deletion already works.
options: A: Yes. Once retention v1.4 and v1.5 are registered, show you a clickable prototype with Delete in 'Your projects'
B: No for now. Account deletion and Archive are enough; revisit later
C: Yes, and add it now behind the switch so it is ready
